title: selectbox always reverts to first item in the options if the options contain arbitrary classes and format_func is used
body:
### Checklist

- [x] I have searched the [existing issues](https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/issues) for similar issues.
- [x] I added a very descriptive title to this issue.
- [x] I have provided sufficient information below to help reproduce this issue.

### Summary

When the options given to selectbox are instances of arbitrary classes **and** a format function is used, the selected option always revert to the first option if another option is selected.

### Reproducible Code Example

```Python
from dataclasses import dataclass
from typing import NamedTuple

import streamlit as st


[USER](frozen=True)
class MyDataClass:
    id: int
    name: str


class MyNamedTuple(NamedTuple):
    id: int
    name: str


class MyPlainClass:
    def __init__(self, id_: int, name: str) -> None:
        self.id = id_
        self.name = name

TypeToTest = MyDataClass
a = TypeToTest(1, "one")
b = TypeToTest(2, "two")
x = {a: "I", b: "II"}


def format_function(s: MyDataClass | MyNamedTuple | MyPlainClass) -> str:
    print(x[s])
    return s.name


s = st.selectbox("selectbox", [a, b], format_func=format_function)
st.write(s.name)
```

### Steps To Reproduce

Run the code above and try to select the second option.

### Expected Behavior

The second option is selected.

### Current Behavior

selectbox always reverts the selection to the first option.

### Is this a regression?

- [ ] Yes, this used to work in a previous version.

### Debug info

- Streamlit version: 1.58.0
- Python version: 3.14.5
- Operating System: Windows
- Browser: Opera, Edge, Firefox


### Additional Information

- If you replace `TypeToTest = MyDataClass` with `TypeToTest = MyPlainClass` the problem also occurs.
- If you replace `TypeToTest = MyDataClass` with `TypeToTest = MyNamedTuple` the problem does not occur.
- If you remove `print(x[s])`, the problem does not occur.

![Views](https://api.views-badge.org/badge/st-issue-15618)

### Issue Analysis

This is a bug in `st.selectbox` where the selection silently reverts to the first (default) option after the user picks any other option, but only when (a) options are instances of custom classes whose identity-based dict/set lookups don't survive a `deepcopy`, and (b) `format_func` performs such an identity-dependent operation (in the repro, `print(x[s])` against an outer dict keyed on the original instances).

**Likely root cause:** In `lib/streamlit/runtime/state/session_state.py`, widget values are returned via `deepcopy(widget_value)` (so user code can't mutate session state). The selectbox then validates this value against `options` in `validate_and_sync_value_with_options` (`lib/streamlit/elements/lib/options_selector_utils.py`) by calling `format_func` on the deepcopied value and checking the resulting string against the formatted options set. If `format_func` raises (e.g., the user's `format_func` does `x[s]` and `s` is a `deepcopy` of a `MyPlainClass` instance without `__eq__`/`__hash__`), the `except Exception: pass` branch falls through and resets the widget to `default_index` (option 0). The same logic in `SelectboxSerde.serialize` falls back to `str(v)` on exception. This format-func-based identity check was introduced in PR #13648 to fix #13646; it works correctly when `format_func` is pure, but breaks when `format_func` itself relies on object identity. For `MyDataClass(frozen=True)` and `MyNamedTuple` the auto-generated value-based `__hash__`/`__eq__` should make the dict lookup survive deepcopy — worth verifying whether the repro actually fails for `MyDataClass` (it might be specific to `MyPlainClass`).

### Related Issues

- [#3703 — Selectbox/radio/multiselect widgets copy option values resulting in index errors and other problems](https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/issues/3703): Same underlying root cause — widgets `deepcopy` option values, breaking identity for custom objects without `__eq__`/`__hash__`.
- [#8008 — Selectbox returns old element not in options if format_func returns the same value for old and new options](https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/issues/8008): Closely related — selectbox uses `format_func` output as the identity key, which conflates display and identity (the same conflation that's biting this issue).
- [#6352 — Selectbox resets selection on visible name change](https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/issues/6352): Related — selection identity is tracked through the formatted label rather than the underlying object, leading to spurious resets.

[USER] thanks for reporting this issue, I have confirmed it. A repro app can be viewed here: https://issues.streamlit.app/?issue=gh-15618

About the analysis and workaround: If I change `format_function` to 

```python
def format_function(s: MyDataClass | MyNamedTuple | MyPlainClass) -> str:
    print(x[s])
    print("No exception was raised in the previous line")
    print(s.name)
    print("The object received has a name, so it's safe to return it")
    return s.name
```

I see all messages in the console (that is, the function does not raise any exception). Still the selection reverts to the first option.
